primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Where any officer or employee of the state, its agencies or its political subdivisions, or any state agency or political subdivision, fails to comply with the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act, any person aggrieved may bring an action, including but not limited to an action for mandamus, to compel compliance. Venue is statutory: the district court of any district in which the records involved are located, or the district court of Lancaster County.

Supplies the underlying sealing duty on which this action rests. The action becomes available where the applicable § 29-3523(3) period has run or its trigger has occurred and the record is still public.

counselFlags: This is an enforcement action, not a sealing petition. It presupposes that the record already should have been sealed under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3523(3) and that an agency has failed to comply. A participant whose case never qualified under § 29-3523(3) has no claim here, and screening must confirm qualification before this route is offered.

Venue is a statutory election: the district court of any district in which the records involved are located, or the district court of Lancaster County. The participant elects between them, and LegalEase does not make that election.

State v. Coble, 299 Neb. 434 (2018) identifies this action as the correct route, in contrast to a motion filed in the criminal case. A participant who has been advised to file a motion in the criminal case should be redirected here.

Mandamus procedure was not surveyed. Section 29-3528 permits an action including but not limited to an action for mandamus, without setting out the procedure. Whether an application and affidavit and an alternative writ are required decides the packet component list, and that question is unresolved. This Petition is drafted as the general action to compel compliance; if the participant proceeds specifically by mandamus, additional components may be required and are not supplied here.

The rule for service on a Nebraska state agency or political subdivision was not surveyed. No certificate of service is drafted and no service method is asserted; confirm the rule with the clerk or counsel before filing.

Nebraska verification: no verification or notarization statute is identified for a § 29-3528 action, and the procedure governing the action was not surveyed. Confirm what the district court requires before signing; the source does not specify one.
Filing fee: no fee is established at source for a § 29-3528 action. No amount may be stated to a participant; confirm with the clerk of the district court.

The order does not reach private data brokers or privately maintained websites. No Nebraska court order under this section will reach a record held by a private data broker or on a privately maintained website, and it does not reach federal or out-of-state agencies. A participant whose real problem is a commercial background-check site must be told this plainly.

The respondent is never guessed. The non-complying officer, agency or political subdivision is named by the participant, because identifying the wrong respondent defeats the action. A participant who cannot identify the non-compliant agency should not proceed alone.

Non-compliance is alleged, never adjudicated. This Petition alleges that the record remains public notwithstanding the sealing duty; it never asserts that a court has found non-compliance, and it never states the respondent's position.

Attorney review is strongly recommended before this action is filed — a recommendation in the source rather than a gate. It becomes a stop condition where the agency contests and appears through counsel, or where the participant needs representation.

statutory_basis.detail: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-3528, § 29-3523(3), § 29-3523(7) and § 29-3527, with State v. Coble, 299 Neb. 434 (2018) for the route decision. Content is asserted only for the provisions the committed mechanism describes.

requested_relief.detail: An order compelling compliance — that is, sealing of the criminal history record information the Act requires to be sealed. The scope is the compliance § 29-3528 confers and no wider; it does not reach private data brokers, privately maintained websites, or federal and out-of-state agencies.

proposed_order.detail: Proposed order compelling compliance, filed with the petition. The operative relief under § 29-3528 is a court order directed at the non-complying entity.

Service rule and filing fee are unestablished and must be confirmed.
